tracks.narration: Close a switch and a capacitor starts filling — how fast does it get there?
Battery V zero in series with a resistor R and capacitor C. Flip the switch, and current starts pushing charge onto the plates.
The voltage across the capacitor climbs along an exponential curve — V of t equals V zero times one minus e to the minus t over tau.
Tau equals R times C is the time constant. After one tau the voltage has reached sixty three percent. After five tau it is essentially full.
Bigger R or bigger C means slower charging. The time constant R times C sets the entire rhythm.
